newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on U.S. Midwest rainfall.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on U.S. Midwest rainfall.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on rainfall in the U.S. Midwest over the weekend that was heavier than expected, traders said.
But trading was slow as the market awaited the release at 0730 CDT Wednesday of USDA's September crop production report.
Pressure also came from the export sector despite news USDA said 110,000 tonnes were sold to an unknown destination.
USDA's weekly export inspection report released early Monday showed corn inspections for the week ended September 5 at 12.106 million bushels, below the 25.483 million inspected the previous week.
Traders said the market was expecting at least 22.0 million to 31.0 million bushels to be posted on the report.
Cargill Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of December and LIT America sold 2.5 million December, the traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 37,000 contracts, down from 49,692 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Rosenthal Collins bought 500 December $3.00 puts and Refco Inc sold 400 December $3.50 calls, the traders said.
Corn futures ended down 2-1/4 cents a bushel lower to up 3/4, with September down 1/4 at $3.62-1/4 a bushel.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, down from 15,291 Friday.
